evals.description: Pure pass-through, invoked via the Skill tool. The skill resolves the workflow YAML to an absolute path (expanding `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` because relative paths won't survive once the workflow runner takes over) and then calls the `Skill` tool with `skill=workflow` and `args="<absolute path> <user args>"`. It must NOT spawn a sub-agent via the Agent tool — a sub-agent comes up with a restricted tool set and the workflow runner can't execute its Bash phases inside it.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-abt-0 && cd /tmp/eval-abt-0 && printf 'projects:
  - repo: acme/api
    tasks: []
' > tasks.yml
evals.expected_output: One Skill tool call with `skill=workflow`. The `args` string starts with an absolute path ending in `plugins/auto-board-task/workflows/auto-board-task.yaml` (no literal `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` remains) and is followed by `tasks=tasks.yml project_url=https://github.com/users/acme/projects/7` (or the same args in some order).

assertions.text: The skill invokes the `Skill` tool with `skill=workflow` — exactly once
The skill does NOT call the `Agent` tool to spawn a sub-agent for the workflow
The `args` string passed to `Skill` starts with an absolute path ending in `plugins/auto-board-task/workflows/auto-board-task.yaml` — the literal `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` must not appear
Both `tasks=tasks.yml` and `project_url=https://github.com/users/acme/projects/7` appear in the `args` string after the YAML path, unchanged
The skill does NOT invoke `gh-project-sync` or `task-agent` directly — they are reached only through the workflow runner

evals.description: Alternate project-ref form (`project_owner` + `project_number`) and a `default_repo`. All three extras must thread through to the `Skill` invocation's `args` string verbatim. The skill must not silently coerce them into `project_url` or drop any of them.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-abt-1 && cd /tmp/eval-abt-1 && printf 'projects:
  - repo: acme/api
    tasks: []
' > tasks.yml
evals.expected_output: Skill tool call with `skill=workflow` whose `args` contains `project_owner=acme project_number=7 default_repo=acme/api` (no `project_url`).

assertions.text: Both `project_owner=acme` and `project_number=7` appear verbatim in the `args` string passed to `Skill`
The skill does not inject a `project_url=` argument that the user didn't supply

evals.description: Validation is delegated downstream. Even though the workflow YAML declares `project_url` / `project_owner` / `project_number` as inputs that `gh-project-sync` ultimately needs, this skill does not pre-check them. It still calls `Skill(skill=workflow, args=…)` with whatever the user supplied; the workflow runner (or `gh-project-sync` itself) is responsible for surfacing the missing-project-ref error.
evals.setup:
mkdir -p /tmp/eval-abt-2 && cd /tmp/eval-abt-2 && printf 'projects:
  - repo: acme/api
    tasks: []
' > tasks.yml
evals.expected_output: Skill tool is still called with `skill=workflow`. Args contains only the absolute YAML path and `tasks=tasks.yml`; any failure is reported by the workflow runner or the sub-skill in its own output.

assertions.text: The `Skill` tool is invoked with `skill=workflow` even though required inputs for `gh-project-sync` are missing — validation is delegated downstream
The skill does not itself print a parsing/validation error about missing `project_url` or `project_owner`/`project_number`
